challenges.name: Dabba Doo Decoder
challenges.description:
We intercepted a note left on a compromised server. It looks like a reference to something, but all we have is this string: ``` MHhEQUJCQUQwMDo5 ``` The first half is a well-known number that's famous for reading like a word. The second half is just a position. Find what the number sounds like, follow it to its source, and bring back what sits at the given position.
Flag format: `oo{...}`
The flag is a single line of text, entirely lowercase, with spaces and punctuations replaced by underscores. For example, Hello, World. would become `oo{hello_world}`.

hints.content: The wiki entry doesn't just give a meaning, it gives a name. Say that name out loud and think about what else it sounds like.

challenges.name: Signals from the Cosmos
challenges.description:
High in the Bolivian altiplano, far from any human settlement, this photograph was taken on a night when the Milky Way burned brighter than usual.
Aliens were there.
They stood beneath that same sky, beside the illuminated rock, and left something behind for us to find. The image is not just a record of the stars. It is a deliberate message from visitors who walked that plateau and chose this moment to make contact.
The transmission is hidden within the photograph. Recover it.
Photo By Thomas Fuhrmann - Own work, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=91415426

hints.content: Sometimes, what meets the eye is only a distraction from the underlying data layers.

challenges.name: First Bytes
challenges.description: A downloaded file won't open. Can you figure out why and recover the flag hidden behind it?

challenges.description:
Can you decode the secret message? ``` ss!wlmjxcgmtlivwcevicmrwigyvi# ```
Flag format: `oo{...}`

hints.content: Compare the fingerprints of flag format with the encoded message.

challenges.name: Small Key
challenges.description:
Something about this public key is seriously wrong... but can you figure out what?
Your mission is to analyse the provided public key, identify its weakness, and exploit it to recover the private key parameters.
Once you've broken the key, find the two prime numbers `p` and `q` used to generate the private key.
Flag format: The absolute difference between the two primes, `p` and `q`, represented in hexadecimal, using uppercase letters.
Flag: `oo{DIFFERENCE_IN_UPPERCASE_HEX}`
Can you crack the key and uncover the hidden flag?

challenges.name: Passive Aggressive
challenges.description:
A sysadmin fat-fingered their password, tried again, and then pulled a file off the office file server. We grabbed a short slice of traffic from the LAN while it happened, but it's buried in the everyday background noise of the rest of the network.
Work out who actually got in, what their password was, and which file they downloaded.
The flag format is `oo{username_password_word1_word2_word3}`, where the secret words come from the first line of the file.

hints.content: Some protocols never bothered with encryption. Try the ftp display filter.

challenges.name: Password Protected
challenges.description:
You've stumbled upon a mysterious executable guarding a secret behind a password prompt. The catch? Nobody knows the password, and the original developer has left no clues behind.
Or have they?
No source code. No hints. Just a binary and a secret waiting to be discovered.

challenges.name: Keygen
challenges.description:
A program checks whether a supplied serial is valid. The original developer left behind an encoded sequence of integers.
Your task is to reverse-engineer the validation logic and recover the correct serial.
You may use Python to automate your analysis. No network access or external libraries are required.

challenges.name: AETHER Stream
challenges.description:
During the last pass of the rogue CubeSat AETHER-7 we captured a continuous encrypted downlink.
The satellite is using a classic Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) stream cipher (radiation-hardened hardware from the early 2000s).
You are given three consecutive packets. The keystream is continuous across them (the LFSR never reseeds).
* Packet 1 and Packet 2 have fully known plaintext (standard beacon + status frames that every AETHER satellite broadcasts). * Packet 3 contains the flag.
Recover the flag.

hints.content: The encryption is a pure stream cipher. XOR the known plaintexts with their corresponding ciphertexts. You will obtain a long consecutive keystream.

The keystream is generated by a single Linear Feedback Shift Register. Once you have enough consecutive keystream bits, the Berlekamp-Massey algorithm will recover both the length and the feedback polynomial.

You only need the linear recurrence relation. After recovering the connection polynomial, use the last L known keystream bits as a sliding window and generate the exact number of additional bits required for Packet 3.

challenges.name: Invalid URL
challenges.description:
``` "EVERY DOOR HAS AN ADDRESS. NOT EVERY ADDRESS IS A URL." ```
Your mission: Decode the message, uncover the hidden destination, and find the page waiting on the other side.
Flag format: `oo{...}` Note: You might need to use some forensic skills for this challenge.

hints.content: The strange string may be encoded, not encrypted. Look for familiar encoding formats.

challenges.name: A Shot in the Daylight
challenges.description:
A railfan stood at the end of a platform of a train station and caught a modern express thundering past. Your job is to work out exactly which train this was.
Find the time the photo was taken (24-hour clock, local time), the service number of the train, the model of train, and the station the photographer was standing at.
Careful: the code on the front of the train is not the service number. That code is like a licence plate, since it names one physical train set. The service number is the identifier the railway gives to a scheduled run, and it stays the same every day that run operates.
Flag format: `oo{HH-MM_SERVICENUMBER_MODEL_STATION}`
Example Flag **(not the answer)**: `oo{17-42_8431_XTRAPOLIS_FLINDERS_STREET_STATION}`
* Everything in capitals, words separated by underscores * Remove all punctuations (hyphens, spaces, etc.) in the service number and the train model part of the flag, and replace spaces with underscore in the train station name. * The station always ends in _STATION * Time uses a hyphen

challenges.name: Needle in the Codestack
challenges.description:
You are given one Python file. Run it and it just asks for a flag. Inspect the source code and you'll find 11 things that all look like legitimate flags, but only one of them is actually checked against your guess.
You do not have to test throuogh every single flags.

hints.content: what are the properties of XOR operation?
